articleTitle: Should You Rehome Your Cat When a Baby Arrives?
imageHeadline: Cat Peeing Before Baby Arrives? Don't Rehome Yet
imageSubtext: See what the behavior actually means and how to fix it
pinTitle: cat peeing in house before baby arrives what to do instead of rehoming
pinDescription: If your cat is peeing in closets or acting out before your baby arrives, it's usually a solvable stress response—not a reason to rehome. Learn what inappropriate elimination actually signals and the practical steps that address the root cause, so you can keep your cat and prepare for baby safely. Get the full breakdown on the site.
